articles.title: Tremendo enfado de Ancelotti y Raphinha, que acabaron expulsados
articles.standfirst: Entrenador y capitán de Brasil se quejaron del tercer gol de los nipones en el añadido y acabaron siendo expulsados por roja directa
articles.summary: Entrenador y capitán de Brasil se quejaron del tercer gol de los nipones en el añadido y acabaron siendo expulsados por roja directa
articles.body: Brasil sigue generando muchas dudas en su juego. En plena gira por Asia y Oceanía, los brasileños cosecharon su primer derrota, esta vez ante Japón, en partido amistoso disputado en Singapur. Los japoneses se adelantaron 2-0 en la primera parte aprovechando los errores en defensa, algo que desquició a Ancelotti. El técnico italiano estuvo muy crítico durante todo el partido, además de Raphinha. El capitán de la canarinha, que no tuvo su mejor día, tuvo varios enfrentamientos con jugadores japoneses y terminó siendo sustituido. Vini empató el partido con un doblete, pero otro error atrás condenó a los brasileño en el añadido, lo que provocó el enorme enfado en el banquillo de la pentacampeona mundial. Pedían una falta anterior que el colegiado no señaló, pese a luego revisarse, y Ancelotti no podía más. El entrenador italiano terminó explotando contra el cuarto árbitro y acabó viendo la roja directa en el 92'. Acto seguido, la roja a Raphinha, que también había dejado claras sus protestas. Los dos a vestuarios y primera derrota de Brasil en esta pequeña gira que está dejando muchas dudas en el juego del cuadro brasileño. "Quiero pedir disculpas por la expulsión, pero es muy complicado no hablar del árbitro", dijo Raphinha tras el encuentro y añadió: “Es difícil cuando estás jugando también contra el árbitro. Eso complica mucho las cosas. No estoy diciendo que no tengamos culpa. Tenemos mucho que mejorar y lo haremos, pero no podemos ignorar la actuación arbitral de hoy”.

articles.title: Deion Sanders Gets Biggest Win as Colorado Upsets Houston, Top Box Score Player Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: Amid growing speculation that he could be on the hot seat, Deion Sanders led Colorado to its first signature win of the season with a 42-32 upset victory over No. 14 Houston in Boulder on Friday night.
articles.body:
Amid growing speculation that he could be on the hot seat, Deion Sanders led Colorado to its first signature win of the season with a 42-32 upset victory over No. 14 Houston in Boulder on Friday night.

The Buffaloes pulled off the win thanks to 249 rushing yards and five touchdowns on the ground. Richard Young led the charge with 99 yards and two scores on 21 attempts.

The victory for Colorado was its first over a team ranked in the top 15 of the Associated Press poll since 2007. It was also the program's first win over any ranked opponent since defeating No. 22 Iowa State on Oct. 11, 2025.

Despite the struggles for Colorado throughout the season, Sanders used his postgame press conference to praise his "resilient" players and explain why he wasn't surprised by this result.

"These kids are resilient," Sanders said. "They have not stopped. They have not quit. They have not given up as well as the coaching staff. I'm really a proud guy right now. ... I still expect a lot more from us. We've been capable of this all season long, but we just hadn't put it together."

After answering questions about his job security following last week's 20-10 loss to the Arizona State, Sanders said on Friday he is unbothered by the talk.

"I've been around noise all my life," Sanders said. "This isn't new."

Houston looked like it was going to dominate early with its first two drives consisting of 28 plays and eating nearly 13 minutes of game time. Makhi Hughes capped off the second drive with a seven-yard touchdown run to make it 10-0.

Colorado responded with touchdowns on three of its four possessions in the second quarter to take a 21-20 lead going into halftime. Young started the scoring barrage with a 38-yard run.

DeKalon Taylor had the longest play of the game with a 67-yard touchdown run on a third-down option run late in the first half.

The third quarter started ugly for both teams with Isaac Wilson throwing an interception on the first play from scrimmage, but Colorado got the ball right back thanks to Randon Fontenette's strip sack of Houston quarterback Conner Weigman.

Colorado took advantage of the turnover with a touchdown on its ensuing possession. It added another score later in the quarter on Kaneal Sweetwyne's 14-yard touchdown to take a 35-20 lead.

The Colorado defense was terrific in the third quarter by forcing two turnovers, a turnover on downs and a punt to keep the Cougars off the board.

Houston's attempt at a fourth-quarter rally came up short because after Weigman's 24-yard touchdown pass to Patrick Overmyer, the two-point attempt failed to keep it a two-possession game at 35-26.

Colorado came right back with a 75-yard touchdown drive capped off by Young's second score of the night to get the lead back up to 16.

The win moves Colorado to 4-6 overall this season with two games remaining to become bowl eligible. It will go on the road next week to take on Cincinnati.

Houston's playoff hopes likely came to an end with this loss, but head coach Willie Fritz will look to get his team back on track against West Virginia on Nov. 21.

articles.title: Oklahoma AD Calls Out Sankey, SEC for Forfeit Threat and Rescheduling Ole Miss Game
articles.summary: Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny is unhappy about the SEC's decision to move the Sooners' scheduled game against Mississippi from Saturday to Sunday stemming from the FAA grounding all flights for a few hours on Friday.
articles.body:
Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny is unhappy about the SEC's decision to move the Sooners' scheduled game against Mississippi from Saturday to Sunday stemming from the FAA grounding all flights for a few hours on Friday.

In a statement posted on X, Denny wrote that SEC commissioner Greg Sankey indicated Oklahoma it would forfeit the game if it refused to go ahead with the planned Sunday start time and cited the "significant impact" changing the day of the game creates for fans planning to attend.

"After multiple conversations with the league office, Commissioner [Greg] Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection. ... He further informed us that our failure to play on Sunday at the directed time would result in a forfeit.

"Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans. Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations, and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment, and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference's decision tonight."

Denny did note the university recognizes the "extraordinary circumstances" created by the ground stoppage and Mississippi "explored every avenue" to get to Norman to play on Saturday, but the Rebels were "unable to find a solution" that would give them enough time.

The SEC said in a statement announcing the change that Ole Miss was "unable to depart" from Oxford and a "late-night departure could not be accommodated" after the the stoppage was. lifted.

Several teams across the country were impacted the ground stoppage, resulting in start times for eight games being adjusted thus far.

The Mississippi-Oklahoma matchup is the only one at this point that is not being played Saturday. It was originally scheduled to kickoff at 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday afternoon.

The SEC's scheduling decision does work against Ole Miss and Oklahoma because they will be playing on a short week in their next games on Nov. 21, but both teams are playing at home so travel won't be an issue on their ends.

Oklahoma will host Texas A&M at Memorial Stadium. Mississippi will take on FCS program Wofford before the annual Egg Bowl against Mississippi State on Nov. 27.

There is currently no update on the broadcasting schedule for the Mississippi-Oklahoma game. It was originally set to air on the SEC Network.

A 1 p.m. ET Sunday kickoff means the game will also be going head-to-head with the seven NFL games that will begin at the same time.

articles.title: Exeter 1-0 Cheltenham
articles.summary: Lakyle Samuel's first professional goal was enough for Exeter to see off Cheltenham 1-0 at St James Park in Sky Bet League Two.
articles.body:
Whether the on-loan Manchester City defender meant it or not only he will know, but his spectacular 51st-minute cross-shot settled an even contest between two sides pushing for promotion.

Exeter fashioned the first opening in the 10th minute when Jack Fitzwater's clearance fell invitingly for Anthony Scully, but he failed to get the ball under control and get a shot away when in on goal.

The Robins should have gone in front in the 18th minute when Pierce Sweeney's knockdown found Shaun McWilliams, but he smashed his shot against the top of the crossbar and out of the ground.

The deadlock was broken in the 51st minute when the ball was played forward by Harry Kite to Samuel out on the right touchline and his first-time effort on the half turn dipped and swerved over the head of Robins goalkeeper Wyll Stanway and landed in the net.

Kite almost made it 2-0 but his shot was just wide of goal, while Charlie McCann so nearly rescued a point in the final minute for Cheltenham, but his stunning long-range shot came back off the inside of an upright.

articles.summary: Xavi desconvoca al centrocampistas por molestias en la espalda
articles.body: Frenkie de Jong abandona la concentración de la selección neerlandesa y regresa a Barcelona. El jugador sufrió unas molestias leves durante el partido de la Liga de Naciones contra Grecia y, por precaución, ha quedado fuera de la convocatoria para el próximo encuentro frente a Alemania del próximo lunes. Así lo anunció la KNVB este sábado por la tarde. De Jong disputó la primera parte del encuentro contra los griegos el viernes por la noche. Ante la ausencia de Virgil van Dijk, ejerció como capitán de los Países Bajos. Xavi Hernández dejó a De Jong en el vestuario tras el descanso. Después del encuentro, el seleccionador indicó que no le preocupaba el estado físico del centrocampista del Barcelona, ya que no había lesión y solo se trataba de unas molestias en la espalda. A pesar de ello, este sábado se decidió que De Jong no participe en el partido contra Alemania. La KNVB alude a «pequeñas molestias» y señala que, «por precaución», el jugador no viajará a Berlín. La situación en torno a De Jong es delicada, ya que llegó a disputar minutos con la selección neerlandesa durante el Mundial a pesar de estar lesionado. Como consecuencia, su club, el Barcelona, tuvo que prescindir del centrocampista durante cuatro meses.
